mainTopic: One teaching from two פסוקים, and the times for judging דיני ממונות, inheritance and דיני נפשות
overview: The amud opens by looking for a case where one teaching is learned from two different פסוקים. The first try, about items that touch the מזבח, fails because רב אדא בר אהבה shows a real difference over a disqualified עולת העוף. רב אשי offers a better example: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא both include one who does זריקה outside, each from a different פסוק. אביי removes רבי אבהו's claimed difference, so this example stands. The גמרא then turns to the משנה: דיני ממונות begin by day but may be finished at night, learned from 'בכל עת' and רבא's resolution of two פסוקים. רבי מאיר disagrees. He compares court cases to נגעים, so cases are judged only by day and not by blind judges, and this leads to the story of a blind judge near רבי יוחנן. The גמרא also explains how רבי מאיר reads 'בכל עת' (a cloudy day) and 'ביום הנחילו' (court rulings on inheritance are by day only). Finally it begins the rule that דיני נפשות are judged by day, from 'נגד השמש'.

steps.title: Only fit items become holy on the altar, learned from 'lambs'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought as a possible example: the פסוק says anything touching the מזבח becomes holy, and 'כבשים' limits this to items that are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Whatever touches the altar becomes holy.' I might think this means anything at all, fit or unfit. So the next פסוק says 'lambs': just as lambs are fit for the altar, only things that are fit become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a possible example of one teaching learned from two פסוקים. This first opinion learns the limit from the word 'כבשים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, the פסוק sounds like it covers everything, even unfit items. The next פסוק mentions lambs, and lambs are fit קרבנות. So the rule is limited to items that are fit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes holy (and must stay on the altar)

phrases.english: "Whatever touches the altar shall become holy"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:37

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי, בֵּין רָאוּי בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי?
phrases.english: I would understand: whether it is fit or whether it is not fit?
The verse says: "lambs"
phrases.notes: שמות 29:38, the very next פסוק, about the daily lambs.

phrases.aramaic: מָה כְּבָשִׂים רְאוּיִין, אַף כֹּל רָאוּי.
phrases.english: Just as lambs are fit, so too only whatever is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the proposed example of one teaching from two פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That a single teaching can come from two different פסוקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'כל הנוגע במזבח יקדש'

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the same limit from 'burnt-offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reaches the same limit, only fit items, but learns it from the word 'עולה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the פסוק says 'burnt-offering'. Just as a burnt-offering is fit, only things that are fit become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא gives the same rule but from a different word in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions seem to agree on the result: only fit items become holy. The only difference so far is the source. That is why this ברייתא looks like a good example of one teaching from two פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who gives the second source

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: "burnt-offering"
phrases.notes: The daily lambs are called an עולה a few פסוקים later (שמות 29:42).

phrases.aramaic: מָה עוֹלָה רְאוּיָה, אַף כֹּל רָאוּי.
phrases.english: Just as a burnt-offering is fit, so too only whatever is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the same limit from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only items fit for the מזבח become holy by touching it; source: 'עולה'.

steps.title: What do both opinions leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly both opinions are excluding.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do both of them exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what both sources keep out of the rule. The answer will show whether they truly share one teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To count as 'one teaching from two פסוקים', both sides must exclude the very same thing. This question checks that.

phrases.english: And what do the two of them exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is excluded by the two sources just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What item both opinions exclude from becoming holy on the מזבח

steps.title: Both exclude disqualified offerings, just from different words
steps.stepSummary: Both exclude פסולין; one learns it from 'כבשים' and the other from 'עולה', so it is one teaching from two sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: Disqualified offerings. One Sage brings it from 'lambs' and the other Sage brings it from 'burnt-offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: both opinions exclude disqualified offerings. Same teaching, two different sources, so this seems to be the example the גמרא wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions exclude exactly the same items, the argument is only about the source. That would make this a true case of one teaching coming from two פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage... and the other Sage

phrases.english: Disqualified offerings.
One Sage brings it from "lambs,"
and the other Sage brings it from "burnt-offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both exclude disqualified offerings; they differ only in the source word.

steps.title: A disqualified bird burnt-offering shows they really differ
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the two opinions differ about a disqualified עולת העוף, so this is not one teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב אדא בר אהבה say that a disqualified bird burnt-offering is the difference between them? The one who learns from 'lambs' says: lambs, yes, but a bird burnt-offering, no. The one who learns from 'burnt-offering' says even a bird burnt-offering is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the example. רב אדא בר אהבה showed the two sources lead to different results, so they are not one teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כבשים' only matches animal offerings, so a bird עולה is outside the comparison. The word 'עולה' fits a bird עולה too. Since the two sources give a different law for a disqualified bird עולה, each opinion is a separate teaching, and the example falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
But didn't he say (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two opinions disagree about whether disqualified animal offerings are excluded. They agree on that. The only practical difference is the disqualified bird עולה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Adda bar Ahava say:
A disqualified bird burnt-offering is the difference between them.
The one who brings it from "lambs"

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָשִׂים אִין, אֲבָל עוֹלַת הָעוֹף לָא.
phrases.english: says: lambs, yes, but a bird burnt-offering, no.
And the one who brings it from "burnt-offering"
says even a bird burnt-offering is also included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 4's claim that both opinions share one teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both sources teach exactly the same thing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two sources produce a different law for a disqualified bird עולה, they are two different teachings, not one teaching from two פסוקים.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the מזבח is not a valid example, because 'כבשים' and 'עולה' disagree about a disqualified bird עולה.

steps.title: רב אשי offers a new example: one who sprinkles blood outside
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a different ברייתא: the פסוק 'דם יחשב לאיש ההוא דם שפך' includes one who does זריקה outside, according to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: as it was taught in a ברייתא: 'Blood shall be counted to that man; he has shed blood' comes to include one who sprinkles the blood. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first example failed, רב אשי starts a new example of one teaching from two פסוקים. This step opens that ברייתא, and the next step gives its second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about slaughtering a קרבן outside the משכן. רבי ישמעאל reads the extra words 'דם שפך' as also covering זריקה outside. The ברייתא will go on to show a second source for this same teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who gives this teaching

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said: As it was taught in a baraita:
"Blood shall be counted to that man;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.english: he has shed blood"
this comes to include one who sprinkles the blood,
phrases.notes: He means sprinkling a קרבן's blood outside the משכן, not just slaughtering it there.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the example rejected in step 5 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A new proposed example: the ברייתא including one who does זריקה outside, starting with רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא becomes the new test case for whether one teaching can come from two פסוקים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא includes the one who sprinkles from 'or sacrifice'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי עקיבא learns from the words 'או זבח' that one who does זריקה outside is also included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the words 'or sacrifice' come to include the one who sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רב אשי's ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל used 'דם יחשב', and now רבי עקיבא uses 'או זבח' to include the one who sprinkles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא now each have a source for including זריקה outside. The two sources come from two different places in the תורה. This sets up the claim that both reach one law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'or sacrifice', the words in the פסוק that רבי עקיבא uses
to include, to add another case to the law
the one who sprinkles the blood (זריקה) of a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"Or sacrifice": this comes to include the one who sprinkles.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8. He means sprinkling the blood outside the מקדש, like the case in רבי ישמעאל's half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב אשי began in step 6 by giving רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא includes one who does זריקה outside, from the words 'או זבח'.

steps.title: What do both opinions include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא are each including.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what are the two of them including?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick question to set up its point: what is the one law both opinions are adding?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like in step 3, the question makes us see the shared result before naming the two sources. This sets up the answer that it is one teaching from two פסוקים.

phrases.english: And what are the two of them including?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what shared law comes out of the two sources given in steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The single law both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא are including.

steps.title: Both include sprinkling, each from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: Both include זריקה outside. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'דם יחשב' and רבי עקיבא from 'או זבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sprinkling. One Sage brings it from 'blood shall be imputed', and the other Sage brings it from 'or sacrifice'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both include זריקה; they only differ in which פסוק they use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions reach the same law: one who does זריקה outside is included in the punishment. Only the source is different. This makes it רב אשי's replacement example of one teaching learned from two different פסוקים, after the first example failed in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling the blood of a קרבן
one Sage... and the other Sage

phrases.english: Sprinkling.
One Sage brings it from "blood shall be imputed,"
phrases.notes: This Sage is רבי ישמעאל, from step 6.

phrases.english: and the other Sage brings it from "or sacrifice."
phrases.notes: This Sage is רבי עקיבא, from step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְרִיקָה. מָר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מִ״דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both include זריקה outside; רבי ישמעאל from 'דם יחשב', רבי עקיבא from 'או זבח'.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: they disagree about one who slaughtered and sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו said there is a real difference between them: someone who did both שחיטה and זריקה outside. רבי ישמעאל gives one חיוב, רבי עקיבא gives two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אבהו say: the difference between them is one who slaughtered and sprinkled. According to רבי ישמעאל he is liable only once; according to רבי עקיבא he is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's example. If the two opinions lead to a different law, they are not one teaching from two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said both opinions give the same result. רבי אבהו says the result is different when a person does both acts: one חיוב or two. If so, this is a real argument, not one teaching from two פסוקים, much like the challenge in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't (he) say? The opening of a challenge from another statement
liable twice, for two separate sins

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abbahu say:
One who slaughtered and sprinkled is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: He means doing both acts outside the מקדש.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת;
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yishmael, he is liable only once;
according to Rabbi Akiva, he is liable twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 9 that both opinions reach the same law.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא teach one law from two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אבהו shows a practical difference (one חיוב versus two for שחט וזרק), so the two opinions do not teach exactly one law.

steps.title: אביי: even רבי עקיבא gives only one liability
steps.stepSummary: אביי already said that even רבי עקיבא gives only one חיוב, because the פסוק 'שם תעלה עלתיך ושם תעשה' joins all the actions together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this: אביי said, even according to רבי עקיבא he is liable only once, as the verse says: 'There you shall offer your burnt-offerings, and there you shall do.' The Merciful One joined all the actions together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו's statement using אביי's answer. Since even רבי עקיבא gives only one חיוב, there is no practical difference after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learns from the פסוק that the תורה put all the actions of a קרבן under one heading. So שחיטה plus זריקה outside is only one חיוב for both תנאים. With the difference gone, רב אשי's example of one teaching from two פסוקים stands.

keyTerms.meaning: wasn't it already said about this? (bringing an answer that was already given)
He combined them, joined them together
the Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the תורה
actions, here the actions done with a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא both include זריקה outside, each from a different פסוק, and according to אביי neither gives two חיובים for שחט וזרק. So this is a true example of one teaching from two פסוקים.

phrases.english: Wasn't it said about this:
Abaye said:
Even according to Rabbi Akiva too,
he is liable only once,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה עֹלוֹתֶיךָ וְשָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״.
phrases.english: as the verse says: "There you shall offer your burnt-offerings, and there you shall do."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:14.

phrases.english: The Merciful One joined all the actions together.
phrases.notes: Since the פסוק puts them all together, doing several of them outside counts as one sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by removing the practical difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a known statement (אביי) showing that the claimed difference does not exist.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא gives two חיובים for שחט וזרק, so the two opinions really differ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי עקיבא gives one חיוב, since the תורה joined all actions together; the example stands.

steps.title: New topic: monetary cases are judged by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: דיני ממונות are judged by day. It also gives a סימן for the next three discussions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Monetary cases are judged by day, etc. (Mnemonic: judgment, answer, incline.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk about one teaching from two פסוקים is finished. Now the גמרא opens the משנה's rule about when דיני ממונות may be judged. The סימן is a memory aid for three topics coming up.

keyTerms.meaning: monetary cases, court cases about money
a memory aid, a short list of key words

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן is not part of the law. It is just a list of key words to help remember the order of the next discussions.

phrases.english: Monetary cases are judged by day, etc.
(Mnemonic: judgment, answer, incline.)
phrases.notes: Three key words, one from each of the next discussions, to help remember their order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of steps 1-11 and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיני ממונות are judged by day.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this rule about the time for judging דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up רבי חייא בר פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the standard request for a פסוק behind a rule in the משנה. The answer will be a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these words? (where is the source?)

phrases.english: From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the time rule for judging דיני ממונות.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר פפא: 'judge the people at all times'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר פפא brings the פסוק 'ושפטו את העם בכל עת' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabbi Chiyya bar Pappa said: as the verse says, 'And let them judge the people at all times.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר פפא answers the question with a פסוק. The words 'at all times' are the source for the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the judges judge 'at all times', so judging may happen even at night. This is the source for the משנה letting a money case be finished at night. The next step asks why the same words do not let the case start at night too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Pappa said:
As the verse says:
"And let them judge the people at all times."
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר פָּפָּא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק 'ושפטו את העם בכל עת'.

steps.title: If any time works, why not start the case at night too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא בר פפא's source. If 'בכל עת' means any time, even the start of a case should be allowed at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, the start of the case should also be allowed at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the source just given. 'At all times' sounds like night is fine for every stage of the case, not just the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a case must begin by day, though the verdict may be given even at night. The פסוק 'בכל עת' seems too broad, because it allows night for everything. So the source proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you said is true)

phrases.english: If so, the start of the case too [should be allowed at night]?
phrases.notes: The words in brackets aren't said out loud, but that's what the question means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source brought in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר פפא's use of 'ושפטו את העם בכל עת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'At all times' would allow night for the start of the case too, which goes against the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: start by day, verdict even at night
steps.stepSummary: Using רבא's contradiction between two פסוקים, the גמרא explains that the day rule is for the start of a case and the 'any time' rule is for the verdict.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבא, who pointed out a contradiction. One פסוק says 'judge the people at all times,' and another says 'on the day he gives inheritance to his sons.' How do they fit together? Day is for the start of the case, and night is allowed for the verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing רבא. He splits the two פסוקים between the two stages of a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ביום הנחילו' teaches that a case needs daytime. 'בכל עת' teaches that night is allowed. רבא says each פסוק covers a different stage, so the start is by day and the verdict can be at night, exactly as the משנה rules.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (How do they fit together?)
The verdict, the end of the case

phrases.english: Like רבא, for רבא pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: 'And they shall judge the people at all times,'
and it is written: 'And it shall be on the day he gives inheritance to his sons.'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:16

phrases.english: How can this be?

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם לִתְחִלַּת דִּין, לַיְלָה לִגְמַר דִּין.
phrases.english: Day is for the start of the case, night is for the verdict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting two פסוקים between two stages of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בכל עת' allows night for every stage of the case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ביום הנחילו' requires day for the start; 'בכל עת' allows night only for the verdict.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the full source for the משנה's rule about when דיני ממונות are judged.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's rule (verdict may be at night) does not match רבי מאיר, and it brings a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new point: the משנה goes against רבי מאיר. It is setting up the next move, where it quotes the ברייתא with his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new branch. Instead of defending the משנה, the גמרא now shows that another תנא holds differently, and his view comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like (not following the view of)

phrases.english: Our משנה is not like רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the משנה's source, the גמרא points out a תנא who disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's rule about judging דיני ממונות does not follow רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר asks: what do disputes have to do with צרעת marks?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר asks why one פסוק puts ריבים (court disputes) and נגעים (צרעת marks) together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: Why does the פסוק say 'By their word shall be every dispute and every mark of צרעת'? What do disputes have to do with צרעת marks?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר opens his teaching with a question about a פסוק. He is setting up his answer that the two topics are compared on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Court cases and צרעת marks look like two separate subjects. Putting them in one phrase seems strange, so רבי מאיר asks what we should learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק say this?
Mark(s) of צרעת, which a כהן must look at

phrases.english: רבי מאיר used to say:
Why does the פסוק say

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל רִיב וְכׇל נָגַע״?
phrases.english: 'By their word shall be every dispute and every mark'?
phrases.notes: דברים 21:5. 'Their word' means the כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן רִיבִים אֵצֶל נְגָעִים?
phrases.english: And what do disputes have to do with marks?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the ברייתא introduced in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What we learn from joining ריבים and נגעים in one פסוק.

steps.title: The comparison: day, no blind people, no relatives
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that the פסוק compares the two topics. Disputes are like נגעים: only by day and not by the blind. נגעים are like disputes: not by relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it compares disputes to marks. Just as marks are looked at by day, as it says 'on the day it appears,' so disputes are judged by day. Just as marks are not looked at by blind people, as it says 'all that the כהן's eyes see,' so disputes are not judged by blind people. And it compares marks to disputes. Just as disputes are not judged by relatives, so marks are not looked at by relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר explains that the פסוק makes a היקש, a comparison, in both directions. Each topic learns rules from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From נגעים we learn two things for court cases: day only, and no blind judges. From court cases we learn one thing for נגעים: no relatives. Since רבי מאיר says disputes are judged only by day, even the verdict, he disagrees with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a היקש), so one topic learns from the other

phrases.english: Rather, it compares disputes to marks:
just as marks are by day,
as it is written: 'And on the day it appears in him,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:14

phrases.english: so too disputes are by day.
And just as marks are not by blind people,
as it is written: 'As far as the eyes of the כהן can see,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:12

phrases.english: so too disputes are not by blind people.
And it compares marks to disputes:
just as disputes are not by relatives,
so too marks are not by relatives.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן looking at the mark may not be related to the person who has it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's question from Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק makes a two-way היקש: disputes are by day and not by the blind; נגעים are not by relatives.
steps.confusionAlert: The comparison works in both directions. Some rules go from נגעים to court cases, and one rule goes from court cases to נגעים. Keep track of which way each one goes.

steps.title: Should נגעים also need three כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that, like court cases needing three judges, נגעים should need three כהנים, and supports this with a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe: just as disputes need three, marks also need three? And there is logic for this: if a person's money needs three, surely his body needs three!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests how far the comparison goes. It suggests one more rule: three כהנים for נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the topics are compared, maybe the 'three judges' rule also passes to נגעים. A קל וחומר backs it up: a money case is less serious than a ruling about a person's own body, so the body should need at least as many.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical (a reasoning argument)

phrases.english: Or maybe: just as disputes are with three,
so too marks are with three?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: מָמוֹנוֹ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, גּוּפוֹ לָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: if his money is with three, is it not all the more so for his body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to stretch the היקש of Step 19 to one more rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the היקש between ריבים and נגעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the היקש holds, and a קל וחומר agrees, then נגעים should need three כהנים like court cases need three judges.

steps.title: One כהן is enough for נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows that a person is brought to אהרן or to one of his sons, so a single כהן may look at נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall be brought to אהרן the כהן or to one of his sons.' So you learn that even one כהן may look at the marks.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the 'three כהנים' idea with a clear פסוק. The comparison does not cover the number of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק beats both the היקש and the קל וחומר. The words 'or to one' show directly that one כהן is enough. So the היקש teaches day, no blind, and no relatives, but not three.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהוּבָא אֶל אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן אוֹ אֶל אֶחָד וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'And he shall be brought to אהרן the כהן or to one, etc.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2. The full פסוק says 'or to one of his sons, the כהנים.'

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן אֶחָד רוֹאֶה אֶת הַנְּגָעִים.
phrases.english: So you have learned that even one כהן may look at the marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A direct פסוק limits the היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נגעים need three כהנים, like court cases need three judges.
steps.terutzMaskana: One כהן is enough for נגעים; the היקש does not cover the number.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר compares ריבים and נגעים: court cases are only by day and not by blind judges, and נגעים are not seen by relatives. One כהן is still enough for נגעים. Because he says court cases are only by day, our משנה (verdict may be at night) does not follow him.

steps.title: A blind man judges near רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A blind man in רבי יוחנן's neighborhood served as a judge, and רבי יוחנן did not object.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a blind man who lived near רבי יוחנן and judged cases, and רבי יוחנן said nothing to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up a question. Something here looks surprising, and the next step will ask about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's silence counts as approval. So the story tells us that רבי יוחנן held a blind person may judge. That fits our משנה, which allows a verdict at night, and it goes against רבי מאיר's comparison to נגעים.

phrases.english: There was a certain blind man
who lived in the neighborhood of Rabbi Yochanan,
who would judge cases,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan did not say anything at all to him.
phrases.notes: His silence means he was fine with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא סַמְיָא דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁבְבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of רבי מאיר's comparison, which bars a blind person from judging, the גמרא brings a story about a blind judge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן allowed a blind man to judge by not objecting.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's own rules seem to forbid a blind judge
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like an unattributed משנה, and an unattributed משנה excludes even a person blind in one eye from judging. So how could he allow a blind judge?
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he allow this? רבי יוחנן himself said that the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה. We learned in such a משנה: whoever may judge may testify, but some may testify and not judge. And רבי יוחנן explained that this includes someone blind in one eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. It uses רבי יוחנן's own rules to show he should have stopped the blind judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two pieces. First, רבי יוחנן rules like a סתם משנה. Second, he himself read that משנה as excluding a person blind in one eye from judging. If even half-blindness disqualifies a judge, a fully blind man surely cannot judge.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows a משנה stated without a named author
Blind in one of his eyes

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: כׇּל הַכָּשֵׁר לָדוּן כָּשֵׁר לְהָעִיד,
phrases.english: and we learned: Anyone who is fit to judge is fit to testify,
phrases.notes: This משנה is in נדה (49b), and it is stated without a name.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁכָּשֵׁר לְהָעִיד וְאֵין כָּשֵׁר לָדוּן.
phrases.english: but there are some who are fit to testify and not fit to judge.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
This comes to include one who is blind in one of his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's behavior in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's silence toward the blind judge
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules like a סתם משנה. A סתם משנה, as he himself explains it, disqualifies even a person blind in one eye. So a fully blind judge should be disqualified.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן relied on a different unattributed משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן followed our משנה, which allows a monetary verdict at night. That shows it does not compare judging to נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found another unattributed משנה: monetary cases are judged by day and may be concluded at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there are two unattributed משניות that disagree, and רבי יוחנן chose the other one, which is our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a blind person cannot judge came from רבי מאיר's comparison of court cases to נגעים. Our משנה lets the verdict come at night, so it clearly does not accept that comparison. Without the comparison, there is no reason to bar a blind judge.

keyTerms.meaning: They finish (give the verdict) at night

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan found another unattributed mishna:
Monetary cases are judged during the day,
and may be concluded at night.
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה. Allowing night shows it does not follow רבי מאיר's 'like נגעים' comparison from earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing source: another סתם משנה disagrees, and רבי יוחנן followed it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every סתם משנה points to the blind man being unfit to judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our סתם משנה rejects the comparison to נגעים, so a blind person may judge, and רבי יוחנן followed it.

steps.title: Why does this משנה beat the other one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן preferred our סתם משנה over the one in נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes this unattributed משנה stronger than that unattributed משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If both are unattributed, why follow ours? The next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule only says to follow a סתם משנה. It does not say what to do when two of them disagree. So the גמרא needs a reason why one of them carries more weight.

phrases.english: What is the strength of this unattributed mishna
over that unattributed mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּהַאי סְתָמָא מֵהַאי סְתָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why, of two conflicting סתם משניות, our משנה is the one to follow.

steps.title: Two reasons our משנה is stronger
steps.stepSummary: Reason one: our משנה follows the many Sages, while the other follows one Sage. Reason two: our משנה is taught in the chapter about the laws of judging.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: an unattributed משנה that follows the many Sages is preferable. And if you want, say: it is because our משנה teaches this rule in the section about the laws of judging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two separate answers for why רבי יוחנן followed our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: the משנה in נדה matches רבי מאיר alone, while ours matches the majority, so ours wins. Second answer: our משנה sits right in the laws of court cases, its 'home' topic, so it is more exact on this point than a משנה that mentions judging in passing.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of several answers)
An unattributed משנה that follows the many Sages

steps.whatToRemember: When two unattributed משניות disagree, the one that follows the majority, or the one taught in its main topic, carries more weight.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
An unattributed mishna that follows the many is preferable,
phrases.notes: The משנה in נדה matches רבי מאיר alone, while ours follows the other Sages.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
It is because it teaches it
in the context of the laws of judging.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: סְתָמָא דְּרַבִּים עֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה wins because it follows the majority, or because it is taught in its main topic, the laws of judging.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר learn from 'at all times'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר, who limits judging to the day, explains the פסוק 'ושפטו את העם בכל עת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: what does he learn from this פסוק, 'And let them judge the people at all times'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי מאיר and asks what he does with a פסוק that seems to say judging can happen at any time. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that court cases are like נגעים, so they happen only by day. But the פסוק says 'at all times.' The גמרא wants to know what this phrase teaches according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And let them judge the people at all times' (שמות 18:22)
What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
this verse, "And let them judge the people at all times"
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?
phrases.notes: Since רבי מאיר says judging is only by day, 'at all times' seems to go against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי וְשָׁפְטוּ אֶת הָעָם בְּכׇל עֵת מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the blind-judge discussion and returns to רבי מאיר's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר explains 'at all times' if judging is only by day.

steps.title: רבא: it includes a cloudy day
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that, for רבי מאיר, 'at all times' teaches that a court may judge on a cloudy day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it comes to include a cloudy day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The פסוק teaches that judging is allowed on a cloudy day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר compares court cases to נגעים. Without this פסוק, we might copy every daytime limit of נגעים onto court cases, including the rule against cloudy days. 'At all times' tells us a court may still judge on a cloudy day.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It comes to include a cloudy day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'At all times' allows judging on a cloudy day, even though נגעים may not be looked at then.

steps.title: משנה: when a כהן may not look at נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that נגעים are not looked at on a cloudy day, or at certain other times and places, because the light makes the mark look different than it really is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: we do not look at נגעים in the early morning, in the late afternoon, inside a house, or on a cloudy day, because a dull mark looks bright. And not at midday, because a bright mark looks dull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from נגעים to show why רבא needed to include a cloudy day. For נגעים a cloudy day is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן judges a נגע by how bright white it is, so the light must be just right. Dim light makes a dull mark look bright, and strong midday sun makes a bright mark look dull. Because cloudy days are ruled out for נגעים, we would have ruled them out for court cases too, and the פסוק teaches otherwise.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, court cases are like נגעים and happen only by day. But 'at all times' teaches that, unlike נגעים, a court may still judge on a cloudy day.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. In weak light, such as a cloudy day, a dull mark looks bright. In strong midday light, a bright mark looks dull. For court cases, the גמרא discusses only the cloudy-day rule: 'בכל עת' teaches that this limit does not carry over to them.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
We do not look at negaim in the early morning,
or in the late afternoon,
and not inside a house,
and not on a cloudy day,
because a dull one looks bright.
phrases.notes: In weak light, a faint white spot can look strongly white.

phrases.english: And not at midday,
because a bright one looks dull.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֵין רוֹאִין אֶת הַנְּגָעִים שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבא's answer in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That a cloudy day is ruled out for נגעים, so a special פסוק is needed to allow it for court cases.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר learn from 'on the day he gives his sons an inheritance'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with the פסוק 'ביום הנחילו את בניו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: what does he do with the פסוק 'on the day that he gives his sons their inheritance'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from a פסוק that mentions 'the day' in the context of inheritance. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר already learned from נגעים that judging happens only by day. So the words 'on the day' in this פסוק seem extra for him, and the גמרא wants to know what they teach.

keyTerms.meaning: On the day he gives his sons their inheritance (דברים 21:16)
What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו״
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir: this verse, 'on the day that he gives his sons an inheritance'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:16

phrases.english: what does he do with it?
phrases.notes: He already learned day-only judging from נגעים, so what is this verse for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַאי ״בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing how רבי מאיר reads 'בכל עת', the גמרא asks about another פסוק that seems extra for him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from 'ביום הנחילו', since he gets day-only judging from נגעים.

steps.title: Inheritances are distributed by day, not at night
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses the פסוק for רבה בר חנינא's teaching: inheritances are distributed by day and not at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for what רבה בר חנינא taught in front of רב נחמן: 'And it will be on the day he gives his sons an inheritance': by day you distribute inheritances, but you do not distribute inheritances at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר uses the פסוק for a separate teaching: inheritances are given out only by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'day' now teaches something about inheritance instead of judging in general. The exact meaning of 'distributing inheritances' is not yet clear, and the next step challenges it.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
The אמורא who taught this in front of רב נחמן

phrases.english: He needs that verse
for what Rabba bar Ḥanina taught
in front of Rav Naḥman:
'And it will be, on the day he gives his sons an inheritance':
by day you distribute inheritances,
and you do not distribute inheritances at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that inheritances are distributed only by day.

steps.title: Does a person who dies at night have no heirs?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects: then only someone who dies by day would be inherited by his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: But if so, then someone who dies during the day, his sons inherit him, and someone who dies at night, his sons don't inherit him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רבה בר חנינא's teaching by showing it leads to a ridiculous result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance passes to the sons automatically when the father dies. If 'distributing' meant the inheritance itself, a man who died at night would have no heirs, which is clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introducing an absurd result)

phrases.english: He said to him: But if so,
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is speaking to רבה בר חנינא.

phrases.english: one who dies during the day,
his sons inherit him,
and one who dies at night,
his sons do not inherit him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teaching quoted in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר חנינא's rule that inheritances are not distributed at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If taken literally, a man who dies at night would have no heirs, which is absurd.

steps.title: Perhaps he means the court's judging of inheritances
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן suggests that רבה בר חנינא means court cases about inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are talking about the judging of inheritances?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a better reading: the rule is about a court ruling on inheritance cases, not about who inherits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves the rule from the inheritance itself to the court process. A court deciding inheritance matters only by day makes sense, and it fits רבי מאיר's view that courts judge by day.

keyTerms.meaning: Judging of inheritances (court cases about inheritance)

phrases.english: Perhaps you are talking about the judging of inheritances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 32 by narrowing what the teaching means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: 'distributing inheritances' means court judgment of inheritance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule is about the inheritance passing to the sons.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about a court ruling on inheritance, which must be done by day.

steps.title: The whole inheritance section is a matter of judgment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that inheritance is treated as a court matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And it will be for the Children of Israel a statute of judgment': the whole section is set up to be a matter of judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא to support his reading that inheritance is a court matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the inheritance laws 'a statute of judgment'. So inheritance falls under court rules, including the rule that courts judge only by day.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And it will be for the Children of Israel a statute of judgment':
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:11

phrases.english: the entire section is set
phrases.notes: He means the whole inheritance section counts as court business.

phrases.english: to be a matter of judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the suggestion of step 33.
steps.raayaObject: That inheritance is a court matter.

steps.title: Three visitors to a sick man may act as a court
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that three visitors may either write the sick man's instructions or act as a court, while two may only write.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב יהודה in the name of רב, who said: If three people went in to visit a sick person, they may choose to write, or they may choose to act as a court. If two went in, they may write but may not act as a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that dividing up an estate can be done by a court, using רב's case of three people visiting a sick man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people form a court, so they can rule on the sick man's division of his property. Two can only serve as witnesses who write it down. This shows that inheritance division can be done as a real court act.

phrases.english: In line with what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Three who went in to visit the sick person,
if they want, they write,
phrases.notes: They write down how the sick man wants his property divided, and sign as witnesses.

phrases.english: if they want, they act as a court.
Two: they write, but they do not act as a court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical case of inheritance handled as court judgment.
steps.raayaObject: That dividing an estate can be done as a court act.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב

steps.title: At night they become witnesses and cannot judge
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits רב's ruling to daytime. At night they may only write, because they become witnesses and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: This was taught only by day. But at night they write and do not act as a court, because they have become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds that the three visitors may act as a court only by day. This is the day-and-night rule for inheritance judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night a court cannot judge, so the three can only act as witnesses. Once they are witnesses, they cannot judge the same matter the next day. This is a clear example of 'judging inheritances by day only'.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught it in the case of
A witness cannot become a judge (in the same matter)
The אמורא who limits רב's ruling

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught this only by day,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּלַּיְלָה כּוֹתְבִין וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין דִּין,
phrases.english: but at night they write and do not act as a court,
because they have become witnesses,
phrases.notes: Since they could not judge at night, they saw it only as witnesses, so they cannot judge it the next morning either.

phrases.english: and a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's ruling to daytime, which shows the day-only rule for judging inheritance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three visitors may act as a court only by day. At night they become witnesses and cannot later judge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a real case where 'no distributing inheritances at night' applies: the court process, not the inheritance itself.

steps.title: רבה בר חנינא agrees: that is what I meant
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנינא confirms that he meant court judgment of inheritances.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, that is what I am saying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר חנינא agrees with רב נחמן's reading, and the discussion ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 'day' in 'ביום הנחילו' teaches רבי מאיר that court cases about inheritance are judged only by day. The challenge of step 32 is fully answered.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what I am saying

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, 'ביום הנחילו' teaches that a court may rule on inheritance only by day. Children always inherit their father, whenever he dies.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, that is what I am saying.
phrases.notes: רבה בר חנינא is answering רב נחמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב נחמן's reading from step 33.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'Distributing inheritances by day' means a court rules on inheritance only by day. This is what רבי מאיר learns from 'ביום הנחילו'.

steps.title: The משנה: capital cases are judged by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that דיני נפשות are judged during the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Capital cases are judged in the daytime, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask for the source of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the daf discussed money cases and inheritance cases. Now the focus moves to דיני נפשות. The word וכו׳ tells us the משנה continues: the verdict must also be finished during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases, where the defendant's life is at stake
'Etc.' The quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Capital cases are judged in the daytime, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say the court must also finish and rule during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section. The inheritance discussion ended in step 37, and the גמרא now returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דיני נפשות must be judged during the daytime.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the daytime rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תורה teaches that capital cases must be judged by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the משנה's rule. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one is disagreeing with the משנה here. The גמרא simply wants to find the פסוק that the daytime rule is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the תורה source of the rule quoted in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that capital cases must be judged during the day.

steps.title: Proof from 'facing the sun'
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא brings the פסוק about hanging the sinners 'facing the sun,' which shows that capital judgment happens in daylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא says: the פסוק says, 'And hang them unto the Lord, facing the sun.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא answers the question with a פסוק about the people who sinned with פעור. They were to be hanged 'facing the sun.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Facing the sun' means in daylight. Since this פסוק describes a capital punishment, it teaches that capital cases are carried out and judged by day. The proof assumes that the word וְהוֹקַע means an execution, and the next step backs that up.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says. It introduces a proof from the תורה
'And hang.' This is a form of the word הוקעה
Facing the sun, meaning in daylight

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya says:
The verse states,
"And hang them unto the Lord
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:4

phrases.english: facing the sun."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'והוקע אותם לה׳ נגד השמש' shows that capital matters are done facing the sun, meaning by day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the תורה basis for the rule that a court may not judge capital cases at night.

steps.title: Asking how we know הוקעה means hanging
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks for a source showing that the word הוקעה means hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: from where do we know that הוקעה means hanging?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks for proof that the word in the first פסוק, הוקעה, means hanging. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי's proof only works if the פסוק describes an execution. The word הוקעה is unusual, so רב חסדא wants to show its meaning from somewhere else in תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: The rare biblical word used in the פסוק
From where? A request for a source

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says:
From where is it derived that hoka'a is hanging?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מִנַּיִין לְהוֹקָעָה שֶׁהִיא תְּלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the key word in the פסוק that רב שימי בר חייא brought in step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source proving that the word הוקעה means hanging.

steps.title: Proof from the hanging of שאול's sons
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proves from the story of the גבעונים and שאול's descendants that הוקעה means hanging.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And we will hang them unto the Lord in גבעת שאול, the chosen of the Lord.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers his own question with a פסוק that uses the same word, where it clearly refers to hanging people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story of שאול's descendants, the same word וְהוֹקַעֲנוּם is used for their execution by hanging. So in the פעור פסוק, הוקעה also means hanging, which confirms that it describes a capital punishment done 'facing the sun.'

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written. It introduces a quoted פסוק
'And we will hang them.' The same root as הוקעה
גבעת שאול, the place where they were hanged

steps.whatToRemember: Capital cases are judged by day because of 'נגד השמש,' and we know that פסוק describes an execution because הוקעה means hanging, as shown in the story of שאול's descendants.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And we will hang them unto the Lord
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:6

phrases.english: in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהוֹקַעֲנוּם לַה׳ בְּגִבְעַת שָׁאוּל בְּחִיר ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41 and backs up the proof in step 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הוקעה in שמואל ב 21:6 clearly refers to hanging, so it has the same meaning in במדבר 25:4.
